definitions.explanation: The Fahrenheit temperature scale, used mainly in the United States. Japan uses {摂氏|せっし} (Celsius) for everyday temperatures.

examples.japanese: アメリカでは{気温|きおん}を{華氏|かし}で{言|い}う。
examples.english: In America, temperatures are given in Fahrenheit.

examples.japanese: {華氏|かし}{百|ひゃく}{度|ど}は{摂氏|せっし}{約|やく}{三十八|さんじゅうはち}{度|ど}に{当|あ}たり、かなり{暑|あつ}い。
examples.english: 100 degrees Fahrenheit is about 38 degrees Celsius, which is quite hot.

notes:
{華氏|かし} is the Fahrenheit temperature scale. The character {華|か} was chosen to transcribe the 'Fah' of Fahrenheit's name. Japan normally uses {摂氏|せっし} (Celsius), so {華氏|かし} mostly appears when discussing the US.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {華氏|かし}{〜度|ど}: ~ degrees Fahrenheit
- {華氏|かし}で{測|はか}る: to measure in Fahrenheit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {摂氏|せっし}: Celsius — the standard scale in Japan
